subject: Re: Decomposing Exhibit E - split SOW, pricing alignment & billing triggers

Subject: Exhibit E split proposal + pricing questions

Hi Tessa —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we discussed internally, the exec team wants the implementation work (inference integration) and the analytics/monitoring work (ML ops dashboarding) split into two exhibits so we can stage billing and delivery. Two ask items so procurement/legal can route faster:

1) Can you provide a conservative change order draft that splits Exhibit E into E1 (Inference serving SOW) and E2 (Analytics & Ops SOW) with independent acceptance milestones?
2) We need clarity on two billing triggers: what counts as ‘production tokens’ versus ‘development/testing tokens’ (we run simulated load tests) and how burst credits are applied when autoscaling exceeds baseline commit.

Attached is our redline of Exhibit E and a spreadsheet with suggested cost partitioning. Hoping to get a rough change-order by EOD Wednesday so we can start legal.

Attachments: [Attachment: Caduceus_SOW_v3.pdf (pdf)], [Attachment: ExhibitE_Proposed_Split.xlsx (xlsx)]

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform Partnerships
Caduceus AI

Lena —

Thanks for the clear notes and the split proposal. We can do the two-exhibit approach; that’s a common pattern. I’ll draft a change-order skeleton that:

- Converts Exhibit E into Exhibit E-1 (Inference serving): baseline capacity, throughput SLAs, acceptance criteria for go-live.
- Exhibit E-2 (Analytics & Ops): delivery milestones for dashboards, alerting handoff, runbook and handover acceptance.
- Adds a definition section that distinguishes production vs. testing tokens and a short formula for how burst credits are consumed and billed.

Karthik and Laura — looping you in for pricing allocation and procurement timing. Karthik, can your team run the cost re-split against their spreadsheet and propose baseline commit numbers? Laura, can we target an internal legal review by Thursday morning so procurement can circulate?

I’ll attach the first-pass change-order draft when ready (probably tomorrow AM).

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@caduceus.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit E split proposal + pricing questions

Thanks Tessa / Lena —

I ran the numbers against the ExhibitE_Proposed_Split.xlsx and attached a short workbook that shows two options:

Option A (Balanced split): 70% of baseline commit to Inference (E-1), 30% to Analytics (E-2). Burst pool remains shared but billed to the exhibit that triggers provisioning.
Option B (Conservative inference commit): 85% / 15% split with a small shared burst buffer (50% covered by Caduceus, 50% by Redwood) for the first 90 days post-launch.

Operational clarifications:
- "Production tokens": any token consumed after the customer toggles the production flag in the Redwood console and after a short warm-up window (30 minutes) following a new model push.
- "Testing/development tokens": traffic hitting inference endpoints with the header X-Redwood-Stage: staging or development; or requests routed to a model version with label 'dev' or 'canary'. These are metered but excluded from production commit for billing.
- "Burst credits": consumed from the exhibit associated with the request (E-1/E-2) until shared-burst pool is exhausted; any overflow is billed at on-demand rate.

I can convert Option B into a change-order draft if Caduceus prefers a conservative approach.

Attachment: [Attachment: ExhibitE_Pricing_Options.xlsx (xlsx)]

-Karthik
Director, Commercial Pricing

• Define the acceptance criteria for E-1 go-live to include a 48-hour reliability window post-cutover where SLOs are validated.

Also sharing procurement’s DocuSign checklist — can Redwood confirm who on your side will be the signer for the change order (name and title)?

Cheers,
